newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech stock mixed, index dragged lower by Komercni.
newsitem.headline: Czech stock mixed, index dragged lower by Komercni.

text.p: The core shares which make up real-time trading on the Prague Stock Exchange were mixed at the daily fixing on Friday, but slight gains in utilities stocks helped balance another sharp fall in Komercni Banka.

The Reuters Prague RPIX index tracking the top 11 shares which comprise the real-time market dropped 4.2 points at the start of the session to 1,031.2, on losses to the largest banking issue, Komercni Banka.
The PX50 index, which measures the top 50 stocks only at the daily fixing and is adjusted once at the close of trade, was up 0.5 points to 505.5.
Komercni Banka dropped five crowns at the fixing but then fell 45 crowns below Thursday's close at the start of real-time trading to 1,650, after similar losses this week.
Dealers said the negative economic outlook and the drain on the economy from recent flooding in the east continued to batter the financials.

"As the economy is not doing extremely well this year it could happen that at the end of the year the quality of (Komercni's) loan portfolio will worsen as well so there will be a need for provisions for covering non-performing loans," Miroslav Nosal, analyst at Patria Finance said.

He said that the outlook for Komercni's first-half results, expected by the end of this month, was disappointing, and net profit could be about "half a billion crowns lower" than last year's six-month net result of 3.059 billion crowns .
"The outlook (for Komercni)... in not that encouraging," Nosal said.
The largest savings bank Ceska Sporitelna was down five crowns in the early real-time session at 275.
A three crown gain to power utility CEZ and a five crown rise in shares of SPT Telecom to 3,620 helped stem the market's losses.
Of the 11-shares trading in the real-time market, eight were posting gains and three losses, but Komercni, the third most-capitalised issue, weighed the market down.

Dealers said trading activity was still dampened by the impact of flooding in the eastern part of the country and forecasts of more rain for the area where production at hundreds of businesses had been shut.
